correctness.rationale: The 14-vertex Heawood incidence graph has 42 connected forbidden triples for Ind_2. Independent local enumeration of all 2^14 masks reproduces 2256 admissible nonempty simplices and f-vector (14,91,322,651,728,392,58). Reconstructed deterministic vertex-toggle Morse matching has 1121 pairs, remaining 1 vertex plus 13 critical fifth cells; checked all 10150 Hasse arcs admit a topological ordering, giving integral wedge∨13 S^5 (no torsion or hidden attaching map). Independently checked order-seven signed fixed-simplex reduced Lefschetz (-13,1^6), so H5 rational character (13,-1^6), Q⊕2Q(ζ7). Source chain-rank programs over F2,F3,F5 independently corroborate, not proof of integral homotopy.

evidence: Deshpande–Singh classify some multipartite, fully whiskered, cycle/path and perfect tree graphs; Abdelmalek et al Theorem 2.7/Corollary 2.10 applies to trees and caterpillars.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither general family contains the Heawood graph. A statement that all chordal higher independence complexes are wedges cannot cover a nonchordal cubic girth-six incidence graph; no dominating theorem identified.

value.rationale: Heawood is the canonical smallest cubic girth-six graph and Fano plane incidence structure, a natural case outside known higher-independence families. Its nonpure complex has surprising pure-dimensional wedge homotopy; the cyclic character is a distinct useful equivariant invariant. A finite exact result can be valuable without a census of all graphs.
